# gnancount

> Count the number of non-`NaN` elements in a one-dimensional ndarray.

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var gnancount = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/gnancount' );
```

#### gnancount( arrays )

Counts the number of non-`NaN` elements in a one-dimensional ndarray.

```javascript
var vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/ctor' );

var x = vector( [ 1.0, NaN, 4.0, NaN ], 'generic' );

var v = gnancount( [ x ] );
// returns 2
```

The function has the following parameters:

-   **arrays**: array-like object containing a one-dimensional input ndarray.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   If provided an empty one-dimensional ndarray, the function returns `0`.
-   The function supports arbitrary strides and offsets, including negative and zero strides.
-   The function supports input ndarrays whose underlying data buffers use accessor protocols.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/ctor' );
var ndarray2array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/to-array' );
var gnancount = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/gnancount' );

var x = vector( [ 1.0, NaN, -2.0, NaN, 3.0 ], 'generic' );
console.log( ndarray2array( x ) );

var v = gnancount( [ x ] );
console.log( v );
// => 3
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
